title: Accounting Services for Startups: Best Solutions for Venture-Backed Companies
summary: Accounting Services for Startups: Best Solutions for Venture-Backed Companies
body_markdown:
For venture-backed companies, accounting is more than keeping the books up to date. You also need to manage corporate tax filings, R&D tax credits, financial reporting, and the growing complexity that comes with raising capital.


That can mean working with multiple providers: one for bookkeeping, another for corporate taxes, and another for your R&D tax credit study.


For a lean startup team, that's a lot of coordination.


That's why some venture-backed companies choose accounting services for startups that combine bookkeeping, corporate tax preparation, and R&D tax credit support in one place.


## **Key Takeaways**


- Venture-backed companies often have more complex accounting and tax needs than early-stage small businesses.
- Bookkeeping, corporate tax preparation, and R&D tax credits rely on much of the same underlying financial information.
- Combining these services can reduce the number of vendors and handoffs your team has to manage.
- When comparing an accounting and bookkeeping service for startups, look at the total cost and what's actually included.
- Fondo combines bookkeeping, corporate tax preparation, and R&D tax credit support for startups in one place.


## **Why Combine Accounting, Corporate Tax, and R&D Tax Credits?**


Your accounting, tax return, and[R&D tax credit](https://fondo.com/blog/why-most-startups-miss-out-on-r-and-tax-credits) study may be separate projects, but they aren't completely separate processes.


Your books contain the financial information your tax preparer needs. Your payroll and expense data can also support your R&D tax credit calculation. Your corporate tax return then needs to reflect the results of that credit study.


When different providers handle each piece, someone has to connect the dots.


That often means sending financial statements to your tax preparer, providing payroll records to your R&D provider, answering questions about expenses, and making sure the numbers used by each provider line up.


For a founder or lean finance team, that can become a job in itself.


With an integrated accounting solution, the process is more connected. Bookkeeping feeds into the R&D credit study, which then supports the corporate tax return.


Instead of coordinating several providers, your team has one place to manage the core accounting and tax work.


## **What Does an Integrated Accounting Solution Include?**


The exact services vary by provider, but venture-backed companies should look for an accounting solution that can support both their day-to-day[financial operations](https://fondo.com/blog/the-financial-systems-you-need-after-raising-capital) and annual tax requirements.


That may include:


### **Monthly Bookkeeping**


Accurate books, reconciliations, and financial statements give your team a reliable view of the company's finances throughout the year.


### **Corporate Tax Preparation**


Your accounting provider should be able to prepare and file the company's applicable federal and state tax returns and help you understand your tax obligations as the business grows.


### **R&D Tax Credit Support**


For startups investing in product development, engineering, or other qualifying research activities, the R&D tax credit can be an important source of[tax savings](https://fondo.com/blog/the-most-overlooked-tax-savings-for-startups) .


The credit calculation can rely on information such as employee wages, contractor expenses, and other eligible costs. Keeping that information organized throughout the year makes the process easier.


### **Ongoing Tax Support**


As your company raises capital, hires employees, or expands, your tax situation can change. A good provider should be able to help you understand those changes rather than only showing up at tax time.


## **Why Does This Matter for Venture-Backed Companies?**


Venture-backed startups already have enough on their plates. Managing multiple accounting and tax providers can add unnecessary work, especially when each provider needs information from another.


Separate providers can also make it harder to see what you're actually spending on accounting and tax services.


A bookkeeping provider may charge one fee. Your CPA charges another for corporate tax preparation. An R&D tax credit provider may charge separately for the credit study.


The monthly accounting price may look reasonable until you add everything together.


That's why it's worth comparing the total cost and scope of services when evaluating accountant services for startups.


## **What Should You Look for in Startup Accounting Services?**


Before choosing a provider, ask:


**What's included in the price?**


Make sure you understand whether bookkeeping, corporate tax preparation, and R&D tax credit work are included or billed separately.


**Who handles the R&D tax credit study?**


Some providers perform the work themselves, while others send it to a separate specialist.


**Do the services use the same financial information?**


Your accounting, payroll, and tax data should be consistent across the different parts of the process.


**How does pricing change as the company grows?**


Ask how transaction volume, headcount, revenue, or additional tax requirements could affect your costs.


**Does the provider understand venture-backed companies?**


Your accounting provider should understand the needs of a company that has raised outside capital, works with investors, and may be spending heavily on R&D.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What accounting services does a startup need?**


Most startups need ongoing bookkeeping and financial reporting. Venture-backed companies may also need corporate tax preparation, tax planning, and support for tax credits such as the R&D tax credit.


### **How much do accounting services for startups cost?**


Costs vary based on company size, transaction volume, complexity, and the services included. Compare the total cost of bookkeeping, tax preparation, and R&D credit services rather than looking only at the monthly bookkeeping fee.


### **Should a startup use separate accounting and tax providers?**


It can, but using separate providers means more coordination. An integrated provider can connect bookkeeping, tax preparation, and R&D credit work and reduce the number of vendors your team manages.


### **Is the R&D tax credit included with corporate tax preparation?**


It depends on the provider. Some charge separately for an R&D tax credit study, while others include it as part of their broader accounting and tax services.


## **The Bottom Line**


For venture-backed companies, accounting, corporate tax, and R&D tax credits are closely connected. When those services are handled separately, founders and finance teams often end up managing the handoffs themselves.
